title: Energy, Work and Power Module 2 Lesson 3: Resistive Friction Work Energy custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A box of mass $12\text{ kg}$ is pulled a distance of $15\text{ m}$ across a rough horizontal floor where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.35$. Calculate the work done against friction. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A block of mass $2.5\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a rough horizontal table. It comes to rest after travelling $16\text{ m}$. Calculate the coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the block and the table. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A package of mass $6\text{ kg}$ slides $10\text{ m}$ down a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the package and the plane is $\mu = 0.25$. Calculate the work done against friction. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A sledge of mass $20\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at the top of a rough slope. The sledge loses $1800\text{ J}$ of gravitational potential energy while descending, and $600\text{ J}$ of work is done against friction. Calculate the speed of the sledge at the bottom of the slope.

A cyclist and bicycle of total mass $80\text{ kg}$ travel along a level road. The cyclist accelerates from $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ over a distance of $30\text{ m}$ against a constant resistance force of $25\text{ N}$. Calculate the total work done by the cyclist.

A car of mass $1000\text{ kg}$ travelling at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ brakes to rest on a level road. The total retarding force (braking plus resistance) has a constant magnitude of $2500\text{ N}$. Use the work-energy principle to calculate the stopping distance.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $50\text{ kg}$ is pulled across a rough horizontal floor by a horizontal force of magnitude $180\text{ N}$. The crate starts from rest and moves a distance of $12\text{ m}$. The coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor is $\mu = 0.28$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the pulling force and the work done against friction over the $12\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the work-energy principle to find the kinetic energy and speed of the crate at the end of the $12\text{ m}$.

questions.prompt: A skier of mass $65\text{ kg}$ starts from rest at the top of a slope of length $40\text{ m}$ inclined at $15^\circ$ to the horizontal. A constant resistance of $60\text{ N}$ opposes the motion throughout. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the loss in gravitational potential energy and the work done against the resistance force.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the work-energy principle to calculate the kinetic energy and the speed of the skier at the bottom of the slope.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $0.75\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at $25^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is $\mu = 0.30$. The particle travels a distance $s$ up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express the gain in gravitational potential energy and the work done against friction in terms of $s$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the initial kinetic energy of the particle, and use the work-energy principle to find the distance $s$.

questions.prompt: A delivery van of mass $1400\text{ kg}$ moves up a hill inclined at $5^\circ$ to the horizontal. The van travels a distance of $200\text{ m}$ along the hill while its speed increases from $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The engine of the van exerts a constant driving force of $2100\text{ N}$ along the hill. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the driving force of the engine and the increase in gravitational potential energy of the van.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the increase in kinetic energy of the van, and calculate the total work done against resistance forces and the average magnitude of the resistance force.

questions.prompt: A sledge of mass $30\text{ kg}$ is pulled from rest along a rough horizontal section $AB$ of length $15\text{ m}$ by a horizontal rope with tension $120\text{ N}$. The coefficient of friction along $AB$ is $\mu = 0.25$. At point $B$, the rope is released, and the sledge continues moving up a smooth slope $BC$ inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal until it comes to instantaneous rest at $C$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy and speed of the sledge as it reaches point $B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the vertical height of $C$ above $B$, and calculate the distance the sledge travels along the slope $BC$.

questions.prompt: A track consists of a straight rough section $PQ$ of length $12\text{ m}$ inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$. Point $Q$ is higher than point $P$. At $Q$, the track transitions tangentially into a smooth curved section $QR$. A block of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is projected from $P$ with speed $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up the straight section $PQ$. The coefficient of friction between the block and $PQ$ is $\mu = 0.35$. The block passes $Q$ and rises up the smooth curve $QR$ to come to instantaneous rest at point $R$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal contact force on the block along $PQ$, and find the work done against friction as the block travels from $P$ to $Q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the work-energy principle to find the speed of the block as it passes point $Q$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical height of $R$ above $Q$, and find the total vertical height of $R$ above $P$.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $3\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $u = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a line of greatest slope of a rough inclined plane of angle $20^\circ$. The particle travels a distance $d$ up the plane to instantaneous rest at point $A$, and then slides back down to its starting point $O$, passing $O$ with speed $v = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By considering the entire round trip from $O$ to $A$ and back to $O$, calculate the total mechanical energy dissipated against friction, and show that the work done against friction on each single leg (up or down) is $71.25\text{ J}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For the upward journey, use the work-energy balance to find the distance $d$ travelled up the plane, and determine the coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the particle and the plane.
